title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a manuscript leaf from Grothendieck's 1965 notes 'Théorie de Galois des motifs'. The neighbouring pages are unrelated: the previous one is a typescript on reflexive modules and Brauer groups by another author, the next is SGA 4-style text on conservative families of fibre functors. They are presumably reused paper or misfiled leaves.

The setting is a Tannakian category of motives, viewed as a gerbe with band (lien) L, where G is the motivic Galois group(oid).

First paragraph. Earlier pages (not seen here) apparently treated a commutative band. They seem to have shown that the corresponding group H, with its weight homomorphism eps: H -> G_m (attached to the Tate motive), has identity component Ker(eps)^0 that is a compact torus. That is, it is anisotropic over R, which is the expected consequence of positivity of the polarisation (Hodge-Riemann / Rosati).

Grothendieck now treats arbitrary, non-commutative G. One can still form the coradical band Corad(L), the abelian quotient band, as for reductive groups G/G^der. It is commutative and corresponds to a quotient gerbe G' with commutative band L'. L' corresponds to a (pro-)torus H, the word probably being 'protorique'. The previous argument then applies to H, so Ker(eps: H -> G_m)^0 is a compact torus. In modern terms: the weight-kernel of the maximal abelian quotient of the motivic Galois group is anisotropic over R. This is the analogue of the familiar property of the connected centre or coradical of Mumford-Tate groups of polarisable Hodge structures, and of the Serre group.

Second paragraph. He now considers a category of motives equipped with a Frobenius, presumably a central element of Aut of the fibre functor or identity functor, such as motives over a finite field, assumed 'geometric'. Then L is commutative and corresponds to a group G of multiplicative type, carrying an element f ('Frobenius'), and G is Zariski-generated by f. This is the motivic Galois group over F_q as the Zariski closure of Frobenius: the Weil-number (pro)torus, Frobenius tori. The text breaks off (struck-out 'Dans le cas qui nous occupe, prenant E ...').
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the statements are plausible sketches.

Implicit hypotheses are not stated on this page: semisimplicity / Tate-type assumptions are needed for the band to be commutative and of multiplicative type over F_q, and a polarisation is needed for the compactness of Ker(eps)^0.

In a pro-algebraic setting, 'engendré au sens de Zariski par f' should be read as density of the subgroup generated by f in the pro-group. That holds by construction if G is defined as the group attached to the Frobenius action (character group = Weil numbers).

ideas.what: Abelianisation (coradical) of the band of a motivic gerbe, giving a quotient gerbe with commutative band corresponding to a pro-torus
ideas.modern_name: coradical / maximal abelian quotient G/G^der of the motivic Galois group; quotient gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (Catégories tannakiennes, 1972); Deligne-Milne (1982); gerbe/band formalism from Giraud
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published works as far as I know; the gerbe formalism is in Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne

ideas.what: Connected kernel of the weight map eps: H -> G_m is a compact (R-anisotropic) torus, as a consequence of polarisation
ideas.modern_name: weight-kernel of the Serre group / Mumford-Tate centre is anisotropic over R (polarisability condition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Serre group), Deligne (Hodge cycles, Shimura varieties), Saavedra Rivano

ideas.what: Motives with a 'geometric' Frobenius: commutative band, group of multiplicative type Zariski-generated by Frobenius f
ideas.modern_name: Weil-number (pro)torus P / motivic Galois group over F_q; Frobenius tori
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972, ch. VI); Langlands-Rapoport (1987); Milne (1994, 'Motives over finite fields'); Serre (Frobenius tori, ca. 1981)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's motive ideas are only sketched in letters to Serre (1964) and Récoltes et Semailles

missed.claim: Early (1965) evidence that Grothendieck already viewed the motivic Galois gerbe over a finite field as having a commutative band of multiplicative type, Zariski-generated by Frobenius, i.e. the Weil-number torus. He also considered the compactness of the weight-kernel of its (co)radical. These ideas are usually traced to Saavedra (1972) and Langlands-Rapoport/Milne (1987-94).
missed.quote: Ainsi L est commutatif et correspond à un groupe [algébrique] multiplicatif G, muni d'un élément f ("Frobenius"), et G est engendré (au sens de Zariski) par f.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution: it documents Grothendieck's role in the Frobenius-torus picture of motives over finite fields that Saavedra later wrote up. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is well-known today (coradical of a motivic Galois group, anisotropy of the weight kernel, Weil-number torus generated by Frobenius) and was developed by Saavedra, Deligne and Milne. Its interest is only historical, as an early Grothendieck formulation, and the page is a fragment that breaks off.
transcription_corrections: 'le {+Lie+} Lie-cov(L)' is more likely 'le lien Corad(L)' (coradical band), with 'lien' inserted above the line.
'isotrique' is likely 'protorique' (pro-torus) or a similar word; 'H' is inserted above, giving 'correspond à un groupe H protorique'.
'Ker(ε : H → G_m))°' is correct; it ends 'est un tore compact' with 'compact' underlined.
'Frobenius Hensel[?] dans Alli-un[?]' is illegible; plausibly 'munie d'un [élément] Frobenius dans Aut(...)' (a central automorphism); the phrase before it is struck out.
'Nous [envisageons maintenant] une [gerbe]' has 'envisageons maintenant' and 'gerbe' struck; the replacement reads roughly 'Nous [considérons] une catégorie de motifs'.
